title: What pediatricians say
summary: The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends swim lessons for children after their first birthday. It says there’s no evidence that swim lessons for babies under 1 lower their risk of drowning. Talk with your pediatrician about what’s right for your child.
points: No swim lesson makes a child drown-proof, at any age.
Lessons are one layer of protection. They never replace an adult watching, fences and alarms, life jackets and CPR.
